blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Chineside

items.t: SSMUH — the rule that actually governs this sub-area's lots: Coquitlam's small-scale multi-unit housing rules allow up to 3 units on lots 280 m² or smaller and up to 4 units on lots larger than 280 m² and under 4,050 m², including secondary suites and carriage or laneway homes; lots not connected to municipal water or sewer fall outside the SSMUH rules. These units are not strata condos and do not appear in condo searches.

blocks.text: Good to know about Chineside

items.t: Coquitlam replaced its OCP in 2026. The Interim Official Community Plan was adopted April 27, 2026 (Bylaws 5511/5512, 2026), superseding the Citywide OCP Bylaw No. 3479, 2001, with a fuller OCP update anticipated to begin in 2027 — planning documents and listing copy citing the old Citywide OCP are a plan out of date.
A zero-sale month is this sub-area's documented shape.

The density story here is suites and carriage homes, not strata. The SSMUH framework (up to 3 units on lots ≤280 m², up to 4 units under 4,050 m²) is the only multi-unit mechanism operating on Chineside streets — which is why a sub-area can be densifying and still have zero condos.

The "Harbour" name search lands in another city. Harbour Place Estates (1872 Harbour Street) is a Port Coquitlam townhouse complex that name-based searches attach to the Chines area; it has no connection to Chineside beyond a shared word.
No Chineside school catchment is verified yet.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Chineside
Fee-simple lots

items.t: Established house lots: detached houses on the central-Coquitlam slope under the small-scale residential zones R-1, R-2 and R-3 in Zoning Bylaw No. 3000, 1996, as the research states them. Lot character, only: subdivision minimums are 650 m² with 18.5 m width in R-1 and R-3, and 465 m² with 12.5 m width in R-2. These are zone minimums, not a claim about any existing lot; the zone and dimensions of a specific lot are UNVERIFIED until checked parcel by parcel. A fee-simple lot carries NO strata, NO Form B and NO strata fees.

Serviced position, as the City states it: Coquitlam utility charges cover water, sewer and drainage and solid waste; lots not connected to municipal water or sewer are outside the SSMUH rules, so property-level septic or well status is UNVERIFIED in the research — confirm servicing for the specific parcel with the City.
ALR vs non-ALR: parcel-level ALR status for Chineside: UNVERIFIED in the sources read; no ALR percentage split is stated. Check any parcel in the ALC's ALR Property and Map Finder.

Watercourse position: the Watercourse Protection Development Permit Area covers all areas within 30 metres of the top of bank or top of ravine bank of any watercourse in this part of Coquitlam; Zoning Bylaw s.519 sets flood protection setbacks and s.523 covers riparian areas. Lot-level status: UNVERIFIED per lot.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Chineside

items.t: Watercourse Development Permit: within 30 metres of the top of bank or top of ravine bank of any watercourse in this part of Coquitlam a Watercourse Protection Development Permit can be required.

Bare-land strata block (for the form — no Chineside bare-land strata plan is verified): Form B diligence (provided within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page); depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws VOID since November 24, 2022 (short-term restrictions may still apply by bylaw); only 55+ age bylaws valid under SPA ss.123.1/123.2, with May 1, 2023 exemptions; a listing's "45+" line is NOT a valid BC age bylaw.

ALR rules (for completeness — no Chineside ALR parcel is confirmed here): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class is three-tiered ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by Oct 31).

faq.q: What sold in Chineside in September 2026?
faq.a: Nothing — detached: 0 solds from 7 listings; condos & townhomes: 0 solds from 0 listings, so no sales ratio applies in either segment. At the Coquitlam community level the detached median sale price was $1,455,000 and the condos & townhomes median was $625,000 (as of September 2026, Source: SnapStats GVR September 2026 report).

faq.q: Which school district serves Chineside, and how do choice programs work?
faq.a: School District 43 (Coquitlam), with address-based catchments checked in the SD43 School Locator. Programs of Choice (French Immersion, Mandarin Bilingual, Montessori) are separate applications, and cross-catchment requests are decided by a lottery / random draw with in-district priority — neither is a catchment entitlement.

faq.q: Are there any condos in Chineside at all?
faq.a: None verified. No condo building or townhome complex name was confirmed on a developer or strata source, and the sub-area recorded 0 condos & townhomes listings in September 2026. A buyer set on a condo is, on current evidence, buying at the City Centre / Burquitlam station clusters or in Central Coquitlam — not in Chineside.

faq.q: Is Chineside in Coquitlam or Port Coquitlam?
faq.a: Coquitlam. SnapStats carries Chineside only under the Coquitlam community, and City of Coquitlam sources place it in central Coquitlam around Austin Avenue and Como Lake Avenue; there is no Chineside sub-area in Port Coquitlam. The city determines the tax bill (due July 2, 2026) and the school district (SD43).

faq.q: Is Chineside the same market as Harbour Chines?
faq.a: In September 2026 Harbour Chines detached sold 3 of 9 while Chineside sold 0 of 7; blending them invents a market neither one had.

faq.q: Can a Chineside house lot add units instead?
faq.a: Yes, under the City's SSMUH rules — up to 3 units on lots 280 m² or smaller and up to 4 units on lots larger than 280 m² and under 4,050 m², including secondary suites and carriage or laneway homes, where zoning and municipal services allow. Those units are not strata condos.

faq.q: Are there any townhouse complexes in Chineside?
faq.a: A buyer set on a townhouse complex is, on current evidence, buying in another Coquitlam sub-area — not in Chineside.

faq.q: Is Chineside in Coquitlam, Port Coquitlam or Chilliwack?
faq.a: Coquitlam — only. SnapStats carries Chineside solely under the Coquitlam community, and City of Coquitlam sources place it in central Coquitlam around Austin Avenue and Como Lake Avenue. The city determines the tax bill (due July 2, 2026, Coquitlam penalties), the bylaws (Zoning Bylaw No. 3000, 1996) and the school district (SD43). Filing it under Chilliwack would put CADREB, Chilliwack bylaws and a different tax calendar on the deal — all wrong.

faq.q: Is Chineside the same market as Harbour Chines?
faq.a: In September 2026 Harbour Chines detached sold 3 of 9 while Chineside sold 0 of 7; blending them invents a market neither one had.

faq.q: What form does the housing here actually take?
faq.a: Detached houses — the fresh listing evidence is houses only, including older stock (listing records show 1958–1977 build years among current Chineside houses) — plus duplexes and the suite/carriage-home units the SSMUH rules allow. The six-neighbourhood profile's "smaller selection of townhomes and condominiums" is a group statement and does not put a named complex inside Chineside.
